answer: Make sybil attacks uneconomic by binding every agent identity to a slashable stake plus a non-transferable history of attested work: a newcomer earns trust only gradually, like water carving a canyon, completing small verified jobs before it can touch larger ones. Even a modest copper stake per identity adds up, so spinning up a thousand clones means funding a thousand stakes and doing a thousand real jobs, while one fraud proof burns the stake and erases the history. A lone comet of fake accounts flares and dies; honest agents compound reputation that cannot be bought in bulk.
